title: Faking versus reading, soul and Sidney Bechet
summary: Braud argues a musician who can read and fake gets work, and says Bechet had soul without reading.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, he could play any. You know what I mean? That makes a good musician. Myself, I studied the bass and trombone. I can play what I have to play my part, and I can fake as well. So that makes the best man. That's what they're looking for. A man can fake and read. You see, a man that can fake and read, he can get a job quicker, because he can better use it. A lot of times, you don't have time to look at music or turn over music. See what I mean? Duke Elliman Band, we made a rehearsal once, and we played the number down a couple of times, and after that, we could do a little more than just looking at the arrangement, because you had to be a little more than a musician. And otherwise, you could use a man that improvised. See what I mean? My success in the music game, I didn't stay up there just playing bass notes. I used it for a guy, you know? I played a voice note in every bar. Then I run my changes. It's coming from a man that knows the instrument, and he can run his changes. All you have to do is know the instrument, then you know what you're doing. You can control it. See what I mean? Yeah. Some, you meet a lot of good musicians, but they're just technical. They're just technical. It's no kind of lift. Understand? Yeah. And so that makes the great artists. Well, and otherwise, we, in the Orleans, we call it soul. That's all. We call it soul. I have a very dear friend of mine. He's from New Orleans, Sidney Bashir. He doesn't read at all. That's right.
But he can play from the Grand Opera down.
